title: Continuous coefficient sheaves preserve a finite lattice sum
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its $\ell$-adic topology and valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ with the subspace topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme], use its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], continuous coefficient ring sheaves $A_T(U)=C(|U|,A)$ and $E_T(U)=C(|U|,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients], and sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $r\geq0$, let $J$ be a nonempty finite set, and let $\Lambda_j\subseteq E^r$ admit $A$-bases that are also $E$-bases. Equip all lattices and $\Lambda=\sum_j\Lambda_j$ with their subspace topologies. The sum map $q:\bigoplus_j\Lambda_j\to\Lambda$ has a continuous $A$-linear right inverse, with the finite product topology on its domain. Consequently, for every topological space $Z$, the map $\bigoplus_j C(Z,\Lambda_j)\to C(Z,\Lambda)$ is surjective. On the pro-étale site of any scheme $S$, the sum of the submodule sheaves $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda_j)$ inside $E_S^r$ is exactly $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda)$. This sheaf is free of rank $r$ over $A_S$, and its inclusion becomes an isomorphism after extension to $E_S$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-sum-lattice] with the given finite nonempty $J$ and its full lattices. Choose an $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $\Lambda$ which is also an $E$-basis of $E^r$. Its coordinate map $\beta:A^r\to\Lambda$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i b_i$, is a homeomorphism. The same lemma gives such coordinate homeomorphisms for each $\Lambda_j$. The hypotheses are exactly those of that lemma, including the product/subspace topologies and the permitted case $r=0$.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: identification of the sheaf sum with the continuous module of the finite sum lattice

proof.text: For each $i$, membership $b_i\in\sum_j\Lambda_j$ gives vectors $v_{ji}\in\Lambda_j$ with $b_i=\sum_jv_{ji}$: group the finitely many summands by $j$, inserting zeros. Define $s_j(\sum_i a_i b_i)=\sum_i a_i v_{ji}$ and $s=(s_j)_j$. These are $A$-linear, and $q(s(\sum_i a_i b_i))=\sum_i a_i\sum_jv_{ji}=\sum_i a_i b_i$, so $q s=1$. Each map $A^r\to E^r$, $(a_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_i v_{ji}$, is continuous: each ambient coordinate is a finite sum of products of a coordinate $a_i\in A\subset E$ with a fixed scalar in $E$. Its image lies in $\Lambda_j$, so it is continuous into its subspace topology. Compose with $\beta^{-1}$ to obtain continuity of $s_j$; finitely many components give continuity of $s$ for the finite product topology. Here the topological field and subspace ring are those of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and the continuity of $\beta^{-1}$ is supplied by [lem-sfb-finite-sum-lattice]. The sum map $q$ is itself continuous by the identical finite-coordinate addition calculation.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: identification of the sheaf sum with the continuous module of the finite sum lattice

proof.text: For any topological space $Z$ and continuous $f:Z\to\Lambda$, put $f_j=s_j\circ f$. Each $f_j$ is continuous into $\Lambda_j$, and $\sum_j f_j=(q\circ s)\circ f=f$. As $J$ is finite the tuple $(f_j)_j$ is an element of the displayed direct sum. Conversely any finite sum of such functions is continuous and takes values in $\Lambda$. Thus the continuous-function sum map is surjective for every $Z$, with no compactness or connectedness assumption.

proof.text: For an object $U$ of $S_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$, postcomposition with $\beta$ gives an $A_S(U)$-linear bijection $A_S(U)^r=C(|U|,A)^r\xrightarrow{\sim}C(|U|,\Lambda)$; its inverse is postcomposition with $\beta^{-1}$ followed by the $r$ coordinate projections. Continuous functions into a finite product are exactly tuples of continuous functions. These maps commute with every restriction because they are postcomposition by fixed maps. Here $A_S$ is the coefficient ring sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-continuous-integral-coefficients]; that $U\mapsto C(|U|,A)$, and likewise $U\mapsto C(|U|,E)$, $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda)$ and $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda_j)$ for the topological abelian groups $E$, $\Lambda$, $\Lambda_j$ (addition is continuous as a restriction of that of $E^r$), satisfy the sheaf condition is [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf]: covering families of $S_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ are fpqc coverings and its fibre products are those of schemes. Thus this identifies the presheaf $F_\Lambda(U)=C(|U|,\Lambda)$ with the sheaf $A_S^r$: the sheaf gluing condition for a finite tuple is checked in each coordinate. In particular $F_\Lambda$ is a free rank-$r$ module sheaf. Apply the coordinate homeomorphisms of [lem-sfb-finite-sum-lattice] in exactly the same way to each $\Lambda_j$ to see that each $F_j(U)=C(|U|,\Lambda_j)$ is a module sheaf.

proof.text: The inclusion $\Lambda\subset E^r$ induces an injective natural map $F_\Lambda\to E_S^r$, and each $F_j$ is contained in it. Apply step 3 to $Z=|U|$: every section of $F_\Lambda$ is a sum of sections of the $F_j$ on $U$ itself. Hence the sectionwise image of $\bigoplus_jF_j\to E_S^r$ is exactly $F_\Lambda$. This is already a sheaf by step 4, so it is also the sheaf image. Explicitly, the map to $F_\Lambda$ has zero sectionwise cokernel, hence zero sheaf cokernel by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; combined with the displayed monomorphism this gives the image factorization. Therefore the sum of submodule sheaves is precisely $U\mapsto C(|U|,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Pushing down by the trace: identification of the sheaf sum with the continuous module of the finite sum lattice

proof.text: Finally let $B\in\operatorname{GL}_r(E)$ have columns $b_i$, using the $E$-basis furnished by [lem-sfb-finite-sum-lattice]. Under step 4 the actual inclusion $F_\Lambda\to E_S^r$ sends the $i$th standard basis section to the constant vector $b_i$. Its scalar-extension adjoint is therefore the matrix $B$ on $E_S^r$, after the elementary identification $E_S\otimes_{A_S}A_S^r\simeq E_S^r$. On each $U$ this identification sends $a\otimes(x_i)_i$ to $(a x_i)_i$, with inverse $(y_i)_i\mapsto\sum_i y_i\otimes e_i$; the two composites are identities by the tensor balancing relation. These formulas commute with restriction, so the presheaf tensor product is isomorphic to $E_S^r$, which is already a sheaf by step 4 ([lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf] for $E$); its sheafification is therefore the same module, and this gives the identification for the sheaf tensor product defined in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Multiplication by $B^{-1}$ is its inverse: its entries are constant sections of $E_S$, and both matrix products are identity matrices. Consequently extension of the inclusion is an isomorphism. For $r=0$ all modules, sums, maps and tensor products in this proof are zero, so the same formulas give the claimed rank-zero conclusions.
